about.title: Hollister Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Hollister's small-town streets — 4th Street, San Felipe Road, and the stretch along San Benito Street — see plenty of foot traffic between shops, ag-related businesses, and neighborhood markets. When a property owner lets a spill sit, ignores a broken step, or ignores poor lighting in a parking lot, someone can end up hurt through no fault of their own. San Benito County's mix of older buildings downtown and newer retail centers means hazards can look very different depending on where the fall happened. Under California law, a property owner or manager generally has to have known, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition before they can be held responsible. That's why documenting what caused the fall — with photos, witness names, and incident reports — matters so much in these cases. If a fall in Hollister left you injured, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who reviews the details and explains your options, free of charge.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises liability claims usually hinge on showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Time Limits Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim, but if a government-owned property in Hollister was involved, that window shrinks significantly. Acting early helps protect your right to pursue a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you're partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault may reduce the outcome. An attorney can help present your side clearly.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall in a Hollister store or business?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the hazard, the surrounding area, and your injuries before anything is cleaned up or moved. Ask an employee to file an incident report and get the names of any witnesses nearby. Surveillance footage often gets overwritten within days or weeks, so requesting it early can matter a lot.

items.question: Does it matter if my fall happened on a weekend afternoon?
items.answer: Reported crashes and incidents in Hollister tend to cluster on Saturday afternoons when foot and vehicle traffic is heaviest, which can mean busier stores and parking areas along 4th Street or San Felipe Road. Busier conditions don't change the legal standard, but they can affect how quickly a hazard should have been noticed and addressed.

items.question: Can I still bring a claim if I wasn't watching where I was walking?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to seek compensation even if you share some responsibility for the fall, though any amount recovered may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can review the specifics of what happened and explain how that might apply to your situation.
